findings.title: Call to non-existent isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() breaks compilation
findings.body: UsernameForm extends UsernamePasswordForm, but the only overload defined (in UsernamePasswordForm) is isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel). The new guard `if (context.getUser() != null && !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled())` calls a no-argument method that does not exist anywhere in the hierarchy, so this will not compile and the whole services module (and therefore the build) fails. It was almost certainly meant to be `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())`.

findings.title: Conditional passkey form only populated when context user is set, breaking initial page / error re-render
findings.body: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel) returns false whenever `user == null`. It is used in authenticate() and challenge() to decide whether to call webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context), which is what renders the `#webauth` form and the `autocomplete="username webauthn"` conditional-UI element. On a fresh login context.getUser() is null, and on the empty/invalid-password re-render the user was only identified from the form (validateUserAndPassword short-circuits before validateUser() calls context.setUser), so context.getUser() is still null. In both cases the conditional passkey UI is no longer populated. This regresses the primary passkey-autofill experience and breaks existing/new tests that assert `username webauthn` and the `#webauth` form on the first page (e.g. PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey lines 145-146, passwordLoginWithExternalKey lines 195-196, webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthentication line 238; PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest.passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey lines 192-194). The gate should depend only on whether passkeys are enabled for the realm, not on `user != null`.

findings.title: Broad catch(Exception) around findElement can swallow real failures and dead fail() call
findings.body: In reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey both "webauth not present" checks are written as `try { assertThat(driver.findElement(...), nullValue()); fail(...); } catch (Exception nsee) { /* expected */ }`. findElement never returns null (it throws NoSuchElementException), so the assertThat(nullValue()) and the fail() are effectively dead code. More importantly, the catch(Exception) also swallows unrelated failures such as WebDriverException from a page that failed to load, causing the test to pass even when the login page is broken. Using Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, ...) (as the sibling PasskeysUsernameFormTest does) expresses the intent without hiding real errors.
